name: Chychkan Gorge
near: There are no villages inside the gorge — only roadside cafés, trout farms and a tourist base. The nearest town is Toktogul (where the gorge opens to the reservoir, ~30–50 km along the highway — not specified); according to OSM, Mazar-Suu is ~23 km in a straight line from the catalogue point.
elev: The gorge's average elevation is about 2,200 m; small lakes on the slopes are at about 3,000 m (too.kg). The cliffs rise roughly 1,000 m above the river (central-asia.live).
short: Chychkan is about 30 km of a picturesque wooded gorge of the river of the same name on the Bishkek — Osh highway between the Ala-Bel Pass and the Toktogul Reservoir: spruce trees, meadows, honey, trout farms and roadside cafés.
desc: Chychkan Gorge stretches for about 30 km along the Chychkan River in the northern part of the Fergana Range (central-asia.live) — from the Ala-Bel Pass south to the Toktogul Reservoir, into which the turbulent river flows (too.kg). The average elevation is about 2,200 m; the slopes are covered with Tian Shan spruce, flowers and berry bushes, and higher up there are small lakes at ~3,000 m. The name translates as “mouse” — because of the many field mice in burrows on the slopes (too.kg). The gorge is known for fragrant honey and medicinal herbs; along the highway there are cafés, trout farms, guesthouses and the Chychkan tourist base (~km 240 of the Bishkek — Osh highway). Part of the territory is the Chychkan state nature reserve (zakaznik). There is almost no mobile coverage in the gorge (too.kg).
guide: Chychkan is the best stop on the long Bishkek — Osh drive: after the bare slopes of Suusamyr and Ala-Bel the road plunges into a spruce forest alongside a turbulent river. Stop for a trout lunch at one of the roadside farms and buy local honey — the gorge is famous for it. If you have a couple of hours, climb up the side valleys — small lakes hide at around 3,000 m. Don't drink water from the river — take it from springs or at a café. There is no mobile coverage, so tell your family you'll be out of touch for a couple of hours.
see: The Chychkan River and spruce slopes along the highway; side valleys (for example, the Itagar River) and high-mountain lakes (~3,000 m); apiaries and honey sales; trout farms; waterfalls, caves and petroglyphs in the surrounding area (central-asia.live — no specific locations); the Ala-Bel Pass to the north and the Toktogul Reservoir to the south.
skip: You're flying Bishkek — Osh and not driving the highway — there's no point in coming here specifically for 5–6 hours. You're looking for secluded places — the highway has heavy traffic. You need mobile coverage — there is almost none here.
diff: Easy: stops by the highway, short walks. Hikes along the side valleys to lakes at ~3,000 m are medium (editorial; too.kg).
when: May–October: the gorge is green and the roadside spots are open (avtoprokat.kg). In winter the highway is passable, but the neighbouring passes (Ala-Bel, Too-Ashuu) are slippery and avalanche-prone.
hours: Open 24 hours (a stretch of state highway); cafés and trout farms mostly operate in the warm season (avtoprokat.kg). The nature reserve regime follows protected-area rules.
daytime: By day — for lunch and a walk; plan to cross the highway's mountain passes in daylight (editorial).
how: Along the Bishkek — Osh highway (EM-02): from Bishkek via the Too-Ashuu tunnel, Suusamyr and the Ala-Bel Pass — about 5–6 h (avtoprokat.kg); the Chychkan tourist base is at ~km 240 of the highway (TripAdvisor). Fee for passing through the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnels: 50 som for cars with Kyrgyz plates / 200 som for foreign ones (since 01.01.2024). From Osh/Jalal-Abad — north via Tash-Kumyr and Toktogul.
needcar: Yes: the gorge is a stretch of the intercity highway. Your own car, a taxi or a seat in a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi Bishkek — Toktogul/Osh (ask to be dropped off in the gorge).
self: Yes: the stops are right by the highway, no permits needed. For hikes into the side valleys — an offline map and a supply of water.
roadtype: A paved intercity Bishkek — Osh highway along the bottom of the gorge; a 4WD car is not required on the main highway in good weather (avtoprokat.kg). Side turn-offs are dirt.
traveltime: From Bishkek — 5–6 h by car (avtoprokat.kg); to Toktogul by marshrutka — longer, with stops. From Osh — roughly 6–7 h (editorial, not confirmed).
stay:
• Chychkan tourist base/hotel (~km 240 of the Bishkek — Osh highway): $51–58 for a standard room, breakfast; TripAdvisor 3.1/5, 10 reviews (2019–05.2026) — people praise the nature and the staff, and criticize the plumbing, dampness and restaurant prices.
• Oson motel — standard rooms and suites, hot water, meals (C.A.T. catalogue, +996 704 663 664; price not confirmed).
• Several guesthouses and many places to camp (too.kg).
net: There is no mobile coverage in the gorge or it is limited (too.kg; avtoprokat.kg). Wi-Fi — in some hotels (not confirmed).
entry: Free: a stretch of highway. You only pay the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnel fee (50/200 som since 01.01.2024), which is unrelated to the gorge.
transfer: Bishkek → Toktogul: marshrutka 400 som, shared taxi 600–800 som/person, private taxi 3,200–5,600 som (toktogulvisit; publication year not given).
bring: Cash for honey and trout; a warm sweater (2,200 m, cool in the evening); water (drinking river water is not recommended — too.kg); mosquito/tick repellent for walks in the forest (editorial).
warn: Do not drink water from the Chychkan River — only from springs or bought. No mobile coverage. Heavy truck traffic — park only on shoulders and pull-outs. In winter and spring avalanches are possible on the Bishkek — Osh highway (video “An avalanche came down on the Bishkek-Osh road”), and the passes are slippery. Trout prices in restaurants can be high (TripAdvisor review: 2,200 som/kg).
food: Fresh trout from local farms; mountain honey and herbal tea from the gorge's herbs (too.kg, avtoprokat.kg). The Oson motel café and the Chychkan tourist base restaurant.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 36 ratings (03.10.2026, the gorge listing). TripAdvisor (Chychkan hotel): 3.1/5, 10 reviews. Pros: nature, forest, river, trout. Cons: service in the hotels, no mobile coverage.
p.sum: Chychkan is a picturesque stretch of the Bishkek — Osh highway between the Ala-Bel Pass and Toktogul: people pass through on the way south and stop for a trout lunch, honey and kumys, and if they wish stay overnight at the Chychkan tourist base (km 240, ~$40–58). By car from Bishkek it is 5–6 h (tunnel fee 50/200 som); without a car — a marshrutka/shared taxi Bishkek — Toktogul or Bishkek — Osh with a stop by arrangement. There is almost no mobile coverage in the gorge.

p.iti.0.plan: 06:00 leave Bishkek → 08:30 Too-Ashuu → 09:30 Suusamyr (breakfast) → 11:00 Ala-Bel → 11:30–13:00 Chychkan: trout lunch, a walk by the river → 14:00 Toktogul → in the evening Tash-Kumyr/Jalal-Abad or a night in Toktogul.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Bishkek → Suusamyr → Chychkan, night at the tourist base. Day 2: a morning walk to the upper slopes → Toktogul Reservoir → (Kara-Suu via Takhtalyk with CBT Toktogul).
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Suusamyr, Ala-Bel Pass, Toktogul Reservoir, Lake Kara-Suu (CBT Toktogul), then Tash-Kumyr → Sary-Chelek.
p.season: June–September: cafés, trout, kumys, camping. September–October: autumn colours. November–April: the highway is open, but the Too-Ashuu and Ala-Bel passes have ice and avalanche danger; many cafés are closed.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka Bishkek — Toktogul 400 som + lunch at a café ~500–800 som + a guesthouse in Toktogul ~1,800–2,300 som ≈ 3,000–3,500 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: Own/rented car ($20–100/day + fuel + the 50/200 som fee) + the Chychkan tourist base $40–58 with breakfast
p.permits: Not needed. Bishkek — Osh highway tunnel fee: 50 som (Kyrgyz) / 200 som (foreign plates) since 01.01.2024.
p.access: Suitable for everyone: roadside stops, cafés. Wheelchair — at the cafés, no trail. With a dog — the Chychkan tourist base is listed as pet-friendly on Casai, but on trip.com “animals prohibited” — check.
